classic-display.purpose: Classic world headings and poster prices — the rounded retail display face, 700–800. Routed via --font-display.

bazar-display.purpose: Bazar world headings, prices, and the phone number — the tariff-chart grotesque.

global-display.purpose: Global world display at weight 900, uppercase, tight tracking — catalogue headline type.

premium-display.purpose: Premium world didone at real scale contrast — huge product names, listing titles up to 6xl.

body-bengali.purpose: Body face for the Bengali worlds (classic, bazar); carries Bengali and Latin in one voice.

body-global.purpose: Global world body — single-family grotesque page.

body-premium.purpose: Premium world body and small tracked caps (0.12–0.18em) for provenance lines, nav, and keys.

shadows.name: shadow-warm-sm
shadows.purpose: Rest — default card state in every world.

shadows.name: shadow-warm
shadows.purpose: Raised — panels sitting on the field at rest.

shadows.name: shadow-warm-md
shadows.purpose: Lifted — hover lift and floating actions.

shadows.name: shadow-warm-lg
shadows.purpose: Overlay — drawers, sheets, and the premium label panel. Tint follows the world's --shadow-warm base.

components.name: Buy Button
components.description: The order action in the active world's --primary buy slot; 48px tall on purchase surfaces.
components.css: .ds-btn-buy { background: hsl(var(--primary)); color: hsl(var(--primary-foreground)); font-family: var(--font-bengali), var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; height: 48px; padding: 0 32px; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-buy:hover { background: hsl(var(--primary) / 0.9); } .ds-btn-buy:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px hsl(var(--background)), 0 0 0 4px hsl(var(--ring)); } .ds-btn-buy:disabled { opacity: 0.5; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Chrome Button
components.description: Secondary action in the world's chrome slot — never a call to action.
components.css: .ds-btn-chrome { background: hsl(var(--secondary)); color: hsl(var(--secondary-foreground)); font-family: var(--font-bengali), var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 600; height: 40px; padding: 0 16px; border: none; border-radius: var(--radius); cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 0.2s; } .ds-btn-chrome:hover { background: hsl(var(--secondary) / 0.85); } .ds-btn-chrome:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px hsl(var(--background)), 0 0 0 4px hsl(var(--ring)); }

components.name: Input Field
components.description: Text input on the 1px world rule; 16px on mobile so iOS never zooms; caret takes the buy colour.
components.css: .ds-input { background: hsl(var(--card)); color: hsl(var(--foreground)); caret-color: hsl(var(--primary)); font-family: var(--font-bengali), var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; height: 40px; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px solid hsl(var(--input)); border-radius: var(--radius); width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 2px hsl(var(--background)), 0 0 0 4px hsl(var(--ring)); }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: Fully rounded means state, never a control — stock tags, discount chips, filter counts.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-block; background: hsl(var(--success)); color: hsl(var(--success-foreground)); font-family: var(--font-bengali), var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.2; padding: 2px 10px; border-radius: 9999px; }

components.name: Price Line
components.description: Universal price anchoring: heavy tabular current price in the buy colour, struck original in muted, savings in the bundle-save slot.
components.css: .ds-price-line { display: flex; align-items: baseline; gap: 8px; font-family: var(--font-bengali), var(--font-inter), sans-serif; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-price-now { color: hsl(var(--primary)); font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.025em; } .ds-price-was { color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); font-size: 0.875rem; } .ds-price-save { background: hsl(var(--bundle-save)); color: hsl(var(--bundle-save-foreground)); font-size: 0.75rem; font-weight: 700; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 9999px; }

components.name: Image Fallback Plate
components.description: A missing or broken product image degrades to a flat plate in the world's muted field carrying the item's initial in the display face — never the browser's broken-image glyph.
components.css: .ds-plate { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 120px; height: 120px; background: hsl(var(--muted)); color: hsl(var(--muted-foreground)); font-family: var(--font-display), var(--font-bengali), serif; font-size: 2.5rem; font-weight: 700; border: 1px solid hsl(var(--border)); border-radius: var(--radius); }

components.name: Product Card Shell
components.description: World-agnostic card shell: card surface on the field, 1px rule, world radius, rest shadow lifting on hover.

narrative.overview:
There is no single house style here; there is a single house contract. The storefront is one chassis — shared routes, shared data actions, shared semantic token slots — dressed by four complete visual worlds, one per template. app/layout.tsx stamps the active template id on <html data-template>, and app/globals.css resolves every semantic token for that world by attribute selector. A component never knows which world it lives in: it asks for bg-primary or border-border and the world answers.

Each world is a real Bangladeshi or catalogue retail object, not a palette swap: the grocer's ruled ledger (classic), the flexiload top-up counter (bazar), the great mail-order catalogue (global), and the apothecary batch label (premium). The worlds diverge hard but obey the same invariants: money is always tabular, the page gutter lives in exactly one place, status is a pill and a pill is never a control, colors resolve only through tokens, broken data degrades in-world, and no surface fabricates a claim the backend cannot back.

Above the worlds sits a third layer: per-client variant overrides injected as a server-rendered <style> using triple-:root selectors, so a client can retint any world without touching code.
keyCharacteristics: Four self-contained visual worlds selected by data-template, all speaking one semantic token vocabulary
A three-rung cascade ladder: :root default → template block → :root:root:root client override
Per-world display and body faces routed through two font variables (--font-display, --font-bengali)
World-tinted shadows (--shadow-warm) instead of neutral black, everywhere
Zoned BD conversion spine (COD, tap-to-call, Dhaka fees) in the Bengali worlds; flat-rate, estimated-date, guest-first spine in the international worlds
Honest data: empty sections collapse, broken images become typographic plates, urgency only when the backend flag backs it

rules.name: The Token-Only Rule
rules.body: Components consume semantic Tailwind classes wired to the CSS variables and nothing else. A hardcoded hex anywhere downstream silently breaks both the world switch and client theming. The one sanctioned raw-HSL surface is bazar's template-owned --dept-1..6 cycle, defined once in bazar.css.

rules.name: The Ladder Rule
rules.body: Three cascade rungs, weakest to strongest: :root (the classic world and default), html[data-template] with dark blocks, then per-client variant overrides emitted as :root:root:root and :root:root:root.dark in a server <style> — present on first paint, winning regardless of stylesheet order. New tokens enter at rung 1, get world values at rung 2, and stay overridable at rung 3.

rules.name: The Same-Slot-Same-Job Rule
rules.body: A world may change what --primary looks like, never what it means. If a design wants a new meaning, it earns a new slot in all four worlds, not a repurposed one.

rules.name: The Tabular Money Rule
rules.body: Every rendered amount uses tabular-nums so price columns and counters never jitter. Currency symbol, separators, and formatting come from business settings and the locale formatter — never a hardcoded string.

rules.name: The Display-Heads Rule
rules.body: h1–h5 inherit the world's display face from the base layer; body copy, buttons, and form labels never borrow it.

rules.name: The Single Gutter Rule
rules.body: The page gutter lives on .container and only there. Adding px-* to a container element doubles the padding.

rules.name: The No-Body-Scroller Rule
rules.body: The viewport scroller is <html>. Nothing may turn <body> into a scroll container: the moment it becomes one, every sticky header resolves against body's scrollport and vanishes on scrolled pages.

rules.name: The Tinted-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No neutral-black shadow utilities; every shadow routes through --shadow-warm so it retints with the world and with client overrides. Physical depth uses real inset shadows and 1px travel — never a halo or a tint change alone.

rules.name: The Pill-For-Status Rule
rules.body: Fully-rounded means 'this is a state, not a control': stock tags, discount chips, filter counts. No world ships pill buttons.

dos: Do resolve every colour, radius, and shadow through the semantic tokens; add new tokens at all three ladder rungs (:root, each html[data-template] block, overridable by variants).
Do keep the buy slot (--primary) the brightest instance of its colour on screen and chrome in --secondary — in every world, the purchase path wins the eye.
Do render money with tabular-nums and the business-settings formatter; BDT for Bangladesh deployments, never a hardcoded symbol or separator.
Do print delivery cost — zoned fees or flat rate — before the order button, and label computed dates "Estimated".
Do degrade in-world: initial-plates for broken images, wordmarks for missing logos, collapsed sections for empty data.
Do keep the gutter on .container alone and the viewport scroller on <html>.
Do keep order CTAs at 48px+ and reachable without hover; the primary device is a low-end Android phone.
Do gate authored motion on prefers-reduced-motion and keep it transform-only.
donts: Don't hardcode a hex, a neutral-black shadow, or a fixed radius in a shared component — it breaks the world switch and client theming silently.
Don't import template runtime code from app/variants/* or middleware; variants reference templates by id only, and the token layer must stay edge-safe.
Don't repurpose a semantic slot for a new meaning, and don't let one world's accent restriction leak into another (each world's DESIGN.md owns its own accent law).

Don't ship pill-shaped buttons, kickers/eyebrows above headings, icon-card scaffolds, gradient text, emoji-as-icons, rotated ribbons, or colored side borders thicker than 1px — the shared refuse-list all four worlds were reviewed against.
Don't fabricate urgency, stock, reviews, or trust claims; if the backend has no field for it, the line does not exist.
Don't add px-* to a .container element or turn <body> into a scroll container.
Don't ship the shadcn default look, the banner-wall marketplace, the Amazon-clone carousel, or the Temu urgency stack — the four confirmed anti-references.
